name: XOR Encoding
description: XORs consecutive values to produce differences. Effective for time-series with small changes between values.

papers.title: XOR-based Compression

name: Delta Encoding (DIFF)
description: Simple first-order predictor that computes differences between consecutive values (also called difference sequence). Effective for monotonic or slowly varying data. A sign-magnitude conversion is often used on the output to produce more leading-zero bits for a modest extra compression gain in subsequent stages. This is equivalent to the 1D lorenzo predictor.

papers.title: Delta Encoding
LC Framework Documentation

name: Lorenzo Predictor
description: Linear predictor that estimates data values based on neighboring values in 1D, 2D, or 3D grids. Uses weighted sum of adjacent values to predict current value, creating residuals for subsequent encoding. Includes variants: mean-integrated, tiled, and second-order.

papers.title: Out-of-core compression and decompression of large n-dimensional scalar fields
papers.authors: L. Ibarria, P. Lindstrom, J. Rossignac and A. Szymczak
papers.note: Original Lorenzo predictor paper and formulation

papers.title: Significantly Improving Lossy Compression for Scientific Data Sets Based on Multidimensional Prediction and Error-Controlled Quantization
papers.authors: D. Tao, S. Di, Z. Chen and F. Cappello
papers.note: SZ 1.4 algorithm - Lorenzo predictor in SZ

papers.title: LC Framework Documentation

name: Paeth Predictor
description: Spatial predictor that estimates each pixel from the byte immediately to its left (a), directly above (b), and upper-left (c), then selects whichever of a, b, or c is numerically closest to the linear estimate a + b − c as the actual prediction — a simple heuristic for picking the best local edge direction. Unlike lorenzo-predictor's fixed weighted-sum extrapolation, Paeth selects among three candidate neighbors per pixel rather than computing a blend of them.
features: Selects among 3 neighbor candidates (left, above, upper-left) rather than computing a fixed weighted sum
Implicitly adapts to local edge direction (horizontal/vertical/diagonal gradients)
One of PNG's 5 per-scanline filter types (None, Sub, Up, Average, Paeth)
Lossless: residual (actual minus predicted) is always exactly invertible

papers.title: Image File Compression Made Easy
PNG (Portable Network Graphics) Specification, Version 1.2
papers.note: RFC 2083 / ISO/IEC 15948 — standardizes Paeth as one of PNG's five per-scanline filter types

verification.notes: New module drafted for the image/video codec expansion (see docs/image-video-codec-scoping.md, Phase 1a). Not yet cross-checked against a specific implementation.

name: Directional Intra Prediction
description: Predicts each block from its already-decoded top and/or left neighbor edge by extrapolating along one of several fixed directions (e.g. horizontal, vertical, diagonal, DC/average), rather than fitting a continuous model to the block's own content. The encoder tries each candidate direction and signals whichever gives the smallest residual. Introduced in H.264/AVC (9 modes for 4×4 luma) and used with progressively richer mode sets in VP8/WebP, HEVC (35 modes), and AV1.
features: Predicts from already-decoded top/left edge pixels, not the block's own content
Mode-selected: the encoder tries several fixed directions and signals the best-fitting one per block
Mode count has grown across codec generations (9 in H.264, up to 35 in HEVC)
Distinct from curve-fitting's regression-fit continuous model and lorenzo-predictor's fixed weighted sum

papers.title: Overview of the H.264/AVC Video Coding Standard
papers.authors: T. Wiegand, G. J. Sullivan, G. Bjøntegaard, A. Luthra
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
papers.note: Introduces H.264's directional intra prediction modes

papers.title: Overview of the High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) Standard
papers.authors: G. J. Sullivan, J.-R. Ohm, W.-J. Han, T. Wiegand
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology

name: Motion-Compensated Prediction
description: Predicts each block from a matching block in a previously-decoded reference frame, found by searching for the best-matching offset (motion vector) within a search window rather than assuming zero motion. The residual is the difference between the current block and its motion-compensated match; the motion vector itself is predicted from neighboring vectors and coded differentially rather than sent raw. The first genuinely temporal (cross-frame) predictor in this catalog — every other Predictor operates within a single frame/array using spatial or sequential-index neighbors. Reference frames are typically the in-loop-filtered reconstruction rather than the raw unfiltered decode, and matches can be refined to sub-pixel precision via interpolation.
features: Searches previously-decoded reference frame(s) for the best-matching block, rather than assuming a fixed spatial relationship
First temporal (cross-frame) predictor in the catalog — every other Predictor works within a single frame/array
Motion vectors are themselves predicted from neighboring blocks and coded differentially, not sent raw
Supports sub-pixel-precision matches via interpolation (quarter-pixel and finer in modern codecs)
Reference frames are typically the in-loop-filtered reconstruction, not the raw unfiltered decode

papers.title: Motion Compensated Interframe Coding for Video Conferencing
papers.authors: A. N. Netravali, J. D. Robbins
papers.note: Early foundational block motion-compensated prediction scheme for video

papers.title: Overview of the H.264/AVC Video Coding Standard
papers.authors: T. Wiegand, G. J. Sullivan, G. Bjøntegaard, A. Luthra
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
papers.note: Describes H.264's quarter-pixel motion-compensated prediction and motion vector prediction

verification.notes: New module for Phase 2 (video codecs, see docs/image-video-codec-scoping.md). Uncontested — no existing Predictor fits a temporal/cross-frame predictor; all others operate within a single frame/array.

name: Spatial Binning Decomposition
description: Partitions unstructured point/particle data into fixed-size spatial grid cells sized directly from the error bound, then represents each particle by (cell id, quantized offset within the cell) instead of a residual from neighboring values. Suited to particle data (molecular dynamics, cosmology, CFD) that has no regular array structure for neighbor-based predictors like lorenzo-predictor to exploit — the cell partitioning plays the role a fixed grid plays for array-based predictors, with the offset quantization folded directly into this step rather than left to a separate downstream Quantizer.
features: For unstructured/irregularly-scattered point data, not regular arrays — the particle-data counterpart to grid-based predictors
Cell size is derived directly from the error bound, coupling decomposition and precision in one step
Represents each particle as (cell id, quantized in-cell offset) rather than a predicted-value residual
Deliberately simple fixed-grid partitioning (O(N)) rather than tree-based schemes (k-d tree, octree), for speed

papers.title: LCP: Enhancing Scientific Data Management with Lossy Compression for Particles
papers.authors: Longtao Zhang, Ruoyu Li, Congrong Ren, Sheng Di, Jinyang Liu, Jiajun Huang, Robert Underwood, Pascal Grosset, Dingwen Tao, Xin Liang, Hanqi Guo, Franck Cappello, Kai Zhao
papers.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Management of Data (SIGMOD 2025)
papers.note: Introduces LCP-S's fixed-size spatial block decomposition for particle data

verification.notes: New module (2026-07-20) for the lcp composition. Description sourced from the SIGMOD'25 paper's LCP-S section (fixed-size blocking, block size = 2×errorbound×p, no sorting/space-filling curve); LCP-T's temporal mode is a separate technique not modeled here.

name: Pattern-Scaling Prediction
description: Predicts each value by matching it against a library of previously-encountered data patterns and scaling the best match, rather than extrapolating from spatial or temporal neighbors — exploits datasets whose values recur as scaled copies of earlier ones due to underlying structure (e.g. physical symmetries), rather than smooth local continuity. Introduced for quantum-chemistry two-electron integral (ERI) tensors, where many entries are exact or near-exact scaled repeats of already-seen sub-patterns.
features: Matches against previously-seen patterns and predicts via a learned scale factor, not neighbor extrapolation
Targets data with repeated-but-rescaled structure rather than smooth spatial/temporal continuity
Reaches much higher compression than neighbor-based predictors on data where it applies (e.g. ~16.8× vs. ~6-7× for general SZ/ZFP on the same ERI data at matched precision, per the original paper)
Domain-specific: introduced for quantum chemistry ERI tensors, not a general-purpose predictor

papers.title: PaSTRI: Error-Bounded Lossy Compression for Two-Electron Integrals in Quantum Chemistry
papers.authors: A. M. Gok, S. Di, Y. Alexeev, D. Tao, V. Mironov, X. Liang, F. Cappello
papers.venue: IEEE International Conference on Cluster Computing (CLUSTER 2018)

verification.notes: New module (2026-07-20) for the pastri composition.

name: Curve Fitting / Regression
description: Fits a polynomial (flat/linear/quadratic/cubic) to each data block via regression, then predicts every point in the block from that one fit. More expressive than Lorenzo for smooth trends and gradients, at higher computational cost. Block size and polynomial order can be fixed or adaptively selected per block.
features: Block-based operation with adaptive block sizing

papers.title: Fast Error-Bounded Lossy HPC Data Compression with SZ
Significantly Improving Lossy Compression for Scientific Data Sets Based on Multidimensional Prediction and Error-Controlled Quantization
papers.authors: Tao D., Di S., Chen Z., Cappello F.
papers.note: Introduces polynomial regression predictors as extension to Lorenzo

name: Interpolation
description: Predicts values between known data points using smooth polynomial curves. There are linear, cubic, and multi-level (hierarchical resolution) variants. Cubic B-splines use piecewise parametric polynomial curves of degree 3, producing smooth second-order differentiable curves at knot locations - particularly effective on sorted monotonic data.

papers.title: Interpolation Methods
papers.note: Standard prediction techniques including spline and multi-level variants

papers.title: ISABELA for Effective In Situ Compression of Scientific Data
papers.authors: S. Lakshminarasimhan, N. Shah, S. Ethier, S-H. Ku, C.S Chang, S. Klasky, R. Latham, R. Ross, N.F. Samatova
papers.note: Cubic B-splines curve fitting for compression

name: Neural Network Prediction
description: Uses trained neural networks to predict data values. Learns complex patterns from training data for sophisticated prediction.

papers.title: Neural Network Based Lossy Compression

name: Implicit Neural Representation (Fourier Features)
description: Fits a small coordinate-based neural network (a multilayer perceptron mapping position → value) to an entire array, then keeps only the trained network weights as the compressed representation — decompression re-evaluates the network at every coordinate. Raw MLPs are biased toward low-frequency functions, so coordinates are first passed through a fixed random Fourier feature mapping (sin/cos of scaled coordinates) to let the network fit high-frequency detail. A distinct technique from generic neural-network-prediction: the network replaces the array outright rather than predicting residuals for a separate quantizer.
features: Data becomes a function (network weights), not a residual-corrected sample grid
Random Fourier feature coordinate mapping overcomes MLPs' low-frequency spectral bias
Encoding is expensive (per-array training); decoding is comparatively cheap network evaluation

papers.title: Fourier Features Let Networks Learn High Frequency Functions in Low Dimensional Domains
papers.authors: Matthew Tancik, Pratul Srinivasan, Ben Mildenhall, Sara Fridovich-Keil, Nithin Raghavan, Utkarsh Singhal, Ravi Ramamoorthi, Jonathan Barron, Ren Ng

verification.notes: Added as the technique behind numcodecs_wasm_fourier_network; no specific implementation confirmed beyond that codec.

name: Downsampling / Pooling
description: Reduces resolution by aggregating blocks of values. Variants include average pooling, max pooling, selective (sparsity-aware), and strided downsampling. Reconstructs via interpolation.
features: Common in neural networks and image processing

papers.title: Downsampling and Pooling Techniques

name: Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT)
description: Frequency-domain transform that represents data as sum of cosine waves. Concentrates energy in low-frequency coefficients, enabling effective compression of smooth data. ZFP uses a near-orthogonal transform in this family. Used in image and video compression (JPEG, MPEG).

papers.title: A Fast Cosine Transform in One and Two Dimensions

name: Hadamard Transform
description: Orthogonal block transform whose basis functions take only ±1 values (square waves) rather than DCT's cosine waves, so it can be computed with only additions and subtractions and no multiplications. Used as a lightweight secondary transform over already-transformed DC coefficients (e.g. H.264's 4×4/2×2 Hadamard pass over luma/chroma DC values) or as the primary luma-DC block transform in VP8/WebP.
features: Multiplication-free: basis functions are ±1 square waves, not cosines
Cheaper to compute than DCT, at the cost of coarser energy compaction
Used as a secondary transform over a block of DC coefficients in H.264
Also used as WebP/VP8's luma-DC block transform

papers.title: A Closed Set of Normal Orthogonal Functions
Overview of the H.264/AVC Video Coding Standard
papers.authors: T. Wiegand, G. J. Sullivan, G. Bjøntegaard, A. Luthra
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
papers.note: Describes H.264's 4×4 Hadamard pass over luma DC coefficients

verification.notes: New module drafted for the image/video codec expansion, Phase 1b (see docs/image-video-codec-scoping.md). Kept separate from dct-transform: different basis functions (±1 square waves vs. cosines), matching the precedent of one module per mathematically distinct transform family (dct/wavelet/multilevel/svd).

name: Wavelet Transform
description: Multi-resolution transform that decomposes data into frequency subbands at different scales. Enables progressive compression and good for non-stationary signals. Used as the decorrelating transform in SPERR.
features: Many wavelet families, each with multiple variants to choose from: CDF 9/7 (JPEG 2000/SPERR's default), biorthogonal (bior, 15 variants), coiflets (coif, 17 variants), Daubechies (db, 38 variants), reverse biorthogonal (rbio, 15 variants), symlets (sym, 19 variants)

papers.title: A theory for multiresolution signal decomposition: the wavelet representation

name: SVD / Tensor Decomposition
description: Factorizes a matrix into singular values and vectors via singular value decomposition (SVD); for multi-dimensional (tensor) data, the Tucker decomposition generalizes SVD to higher-order arrays, factorizing the tensor into a small core tensor plus one factor matrix per dimension. The factorization itself is exact when all components are retained. Compression is achieved by retaining only the dominant components (rank truncation), a downstream/config-level choice rather than an inherent part of the decomposition.
features: Rank reduction via dominant singular values
Tucker/HOSVD generalizes SVD to N-D tensors
Good for smooth, structured multi-dimensional data

papers.title: Singular value decomposition and least squares solutions
papers.authors: G. H. Golub and C. Reinsch
papers.note: Widely used SVD algorithm and numerical method

papers.title: A Multilinear Singular Value Decomposition
papers.authors: L. De Lathauwer, B. De Moor, J. Vandewalle
papers.note: Foundational HOSVD paper — Tucker/HOSVD generalization of SVD to tensors

papers.title: TZ: Achieving High-Ratio Scientific Data Compression on GPUs with Global Data Decomposition
papers.authors: Zhuoxun Yang, Ruoyu Li, Amit Subrahmanya, Vishwas Rao, Sheng Di, Robert Underwood, Longtao Zhang, Jinyang Liu, Franck Cappello, Kai Zhao
papers.note: HPDC '26 — GPU compressor using global Tucker decomposition (ST-HOSVD) via an adaptive randomized SVD, in place of block-wise spatial decomposition

verification.notes: renamed from tucker-decomposition and generalized to SVD, 2026-07-05; TZ compressor citation added 2026-07-15 (HPDC '26, DOI 10.1145/3806645.3807811)

name: Random Projection
description: Projects high-dimensional data onto a lower-dimensional subspace using a random projection matrix, exploiting the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma: with high probability, pairwise distances between points are approximately preserved by a projection into a much lower dimension than the data's original size suggests is possible. Unlike SVD/PCA, the projection matrix is fixed and data-independent, so it costs nothing to compute per-array — only to generate once and store/regenerate from a seed.
features: Data-independent projection matrix (no fitting step, unlike SVD/PCA)
Much cheaper to compute than SVD for high-dimensional data
Dimensionality reduction is inherently lossy — original data is not recoverable exactly

papers.title: Extensions of Lipschitz mappings into a Hilbert space
papers.note: Foundational Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma underlying random projection's distance-preservation guarantee

verification.notes: Added as the technique behind numcodecs_wasm_random_projection; no specific implementation confirmed beyond that codec.

name: Multilevel Decomposition
description: Hierarchical decomposition based on multigrid methods that represents data at multiple levels of resolution. Creates a hierarchy of coefficients where each level captures different scales of variation in the data. Used in MGARD (its flagship component) for adaptive reduction with error control: the multilevel structure enables error bounds in the L-infinity or L2 norm and supports progressive, adaptable retrieval at multiple resolution levels. Works best on smooth continuous fields such as PDE solutions, where it delivers strong rate-distortion performance.
features: Supports multi-dimensional, single-dimensional, or hybrid modes

papers.title: MGARD+: Optimizing Multilevel Methods for Error-bounded Scientific Data Reduction
Multilevel Techniques for Compression and Reduction of Scientific Data
papers.note: Thesis on multilevel methods for scientific data compression

name: Bit Truncation
description: Removes least significant bits from floating-point mantissa. Simple lossy quantization by dropping precision bits.

papers.title: Bit Truncation Methods

name: Stochastic Rounding
description: Rounds each value to one of its two nearest representable values (e.g. quantization bins, or lower-precision floats) with probability proportional to its distance from each — rather than always rounding to the nearest one deterministically. Unbiased in expectation: rounding error doesn't accumulate a systematic drift the way deterministic round-to-nearest can under repeated/iterative application, at the cost of adding per-value variance.
features: Unbiased in expectation — no systematic drift under repeated application
Trades a variance increase for eliminating rounding bias
Common in low-precision ML training (gradient accumulation) and iterative solvers

papers.title: Deep Learning with Limited Numerical Precision
papers.authors: Suyog Gupta, Ankur Agrawal, Kailash Gopalakrishnan, Pritish Narayanan
papers.note: Popularized stochastic rounding for low-precision training; the bias-avoidance argument applies equally to compression quantizers

verification.notes: Added as the technique behind numcodecs_wasm_stochastic_rounding; no specific implementation confirmed beyond that codec.

name: Bit Grooming
description: Bitwise quantization that zeroes least-significant bits in floating-point mantissa to improve compressibility while preserving significant digits (NSD mode).

papers.title: Bit Grooming: Statistically accurate precision-preserving quantization with compression

name: Error-Bounded Quantizer
description: Maps each value to an integer code under a user-chosen error bound — the core lossy step in prediction-based compressors. Supports multiple error-bound modes (ABS, NOA, REL, pseudo-REL) that trade accuracy against how the bound scales with the data.
features: Multiple error modes: ABS, NOA, REL, pseudo-REL
Per-point error guaranteed under the chosen bound
Integer codes suited to entropy coding downstream
Range-relative (NOA) adapts the bound to the data span

papers.title: LC Framework Documentation

name: Linear Quantization
description: Uniform quantization that divides value range into equal-sized bins. Maps continuous values to discrete levels with predictable error bounds and compression ratios.

papers.title: Quantization
papers.note: Standard technique in signal processing literature

name: Log-Scale Quantization
description: Quantizes values into bins whose width grows logarithmically with magnitude rather than staying constant — coarser steps for large values, finer steps near zero — so relative precision stays roughly constant across a wide dynamic range instead of a fixed linear step size wasting bits on small values. Classic form: companding (compress logarithmically, quantize uniformly, then expand on decode), as in μ-law/A-law telephony (ITU-T G.711).
features: Bin width grows with magnitude (roughly constant *relative* precision) rather than a constant absolute step size
Well-suited to wide-dynamic-range data where small values matter as much as large ones
Classic real-world form: companding — compress logarithmically, quantize uniformly, expand back on decode
Distinct from log-scaling (a Mutator/rescaling preprocessing step) — this module is itself the lossy quantization step, not a preprocessing pass ahead of a separate quantizer

papers.title: Pulse Code Modulation (PCM) of Voice Frequencies
papers.note: ITU-T Recommendation G.711 — standardizes μ-law and A-law logarithmic companding, the canonical real-world example of log-scale quantization

verification.notes: New module (2026-07-20), requested directly rather than surfaced from a specific composition. Primary citation (G.711 companding) is from telecom/audio, not scientific HPC compression — flag if a more domain-specific citation is preferred; the technique itself is a legitimate general Quantizer distinct from linear-quantization.

name: Vector Quantization
description: Quantizes vectors rather than scalars. Uses codebook of representative vectors for block-based compression.

papers.title: Vector Quantization

name: Twos-Complement to Magnitude-Sign (TCMS)
description: Converts each value from twos-complement to magnitude-sign representation. Produces more leading zero bits, improving compressibility for subsequent stages.

papers.title: LC Framework Documentation

name: Zigzag Encoding
description: Maps a signed integer to an unsigned integer by doubling the absolute value and subtracting 1 when the original value was negative. Small-magnitude values, positive or negative, map to small unsigned codes. This produces very similar output to TCMS (identical for positive values, slightly different for negative values).
features: Doubles magnitude, interleaves sign into the low bit
Small |n| maps to a small unsigned code regardless of sign

papers.title: Making All Your Integers Positive with Zigzag Encoding
papers.note: Blog post detailing the zigzag encoding technique.

verification.notes: New module split from zigzag-ordering, 2026-07-07. FZGM's ZigzagStage was previously misassigned to zigzag-ordering (a distinct scan-order technique); corrected to this module.

name: Negabinary Signed-to-Unsigned Map
description: Element-wise negabinary (base −2) representation: maps signed integers to an unsigned base-(−2) encoding. Like TCMS and zigzag's value-mapping sense, this reshapes a signed residual stream so small-magnitude values (positive or negative) produce more high-order zero/repeated bits.

verification.notes: generalized from FZGM implementation card; negabinary origin paper is a best-effort, unverified citation

name: IEEE-754 Field Reorder
description: De-biases the IEEE-754 floating-point exponent and reorders the sign/exponent/fraction fields into a fixed byte layout, grouping similar field types together across values to improve downstream compressibility. Two field orders are used in practice: exponent-fraction-sign (EFS) and exponent-sign-fraction (ESF); the exponent de-biasing is identical, only the byte order of the reassembled fields differs.
features: Field reordering variants: EFS and ESF byte layouts
Groups similar field types for better downstream entropy coding

papers.title: LC Framework Documentation

verification.notes: merged from dbefs-mutator (EFS) + dbesf-mutator (ESF), 2026-07-05

name: Fixed-Point Conversion
description: Converts floating-point values to a fixed-point integer representation (a deterministic ldexp-style scale) for bit-exact, platform-independent reproducibility. Unlike error-bound quantization, this is a lossless representation change within the chosen fixed-point range, not a binning step tied to an error tolerance.
features: No error bound involved -- exact within representable range

verification.notes: New module created 2026-07-13 from FZ CPU Module Library's catalog (FixedPointQuantizer page); no exact prior Z-Hub module matched.

name: Logarithmic Scaling
description: Applies logarithmic scaling to compress dynamic range. Effective for data spanning multiple orders of magnitude.

papers.title: Log Transform

name: Inverse Hyperbolic Sine (asinh) Scaling
description: Applies asinh(x) = ln(x + sqrt(x^2 + 1)) to compress dynamic range, the same way log-scaling does — but asinh is defined and smooth across all real numbers (positive, negative, and zero), where plain log-scaling breaks down (undefined for x <= 0). Behaves like a signed log for large |x| while staying linear near zero.
features: Defined for negative values and zero, unlike a plain log transform
Approximately linear near zero, approximately logarithmic for large |x|

verification.notes: Added as the technique behind numcodecs_wasm_asinh; no dedicated paper found (a standard signed generalization of log-scaling), no specific implementation confirmed beyond that codec.

name: Uniform Noise Dithering
description: Adds independent, uniformly-distributed noise to each value before quantization. The added noise decorrelates the quantization error from the input signal, converting the structured, signal-dependent error patterns (banding, contouring) a deterministic quantizer produces into unstructured noise — at the cost of a small increase in overall error magnitude.
features: Decorrelates quantization error from the input signal
Trades structured error (banding/contouring) for unstructured noise
Applied before quantization, not as a replacement for it
Classic technique from audio/image dithering, applicable to scientific quantizers too

papers.title: Theory of Dithered Quantization
papers.authors: Robert M. Gray, Thomas G. Stockham Jr.
papers.note: Foundational analysis of dithering's effect on quantization error

verification.notes: Added as the technique behind numcodecs_wasm_uniform_noise; no specific implementation confirmed beyond that codec.

name: Move-to-Front Transform
description: Maintains list of symbols and moves recently used symbols to front. Produces small values for repeated symbols, improving compression.
features: Produces small numbers for repeated access

papers.title: Move-to-Front Transform

name: Block-Floating-Point Transform
description: Represents a block of floating-point values with a single shared exponent and individual mantissas. Efficiently encodes zero blocks with a single bit. Reduces redundancy by factoring out the common exponent component across spatially correlated values.

papers.title: Fixed-Rate Compressed Floating-Point Arrays

name: Data Normalization
description: Scales data to standard range (e.g., [0,1] or [-1,1]). Improves compressibility and numerical stability.

papers.title: Data Normalization Techniques

name: Color-Space Transform
description: Converts each pixel's color representation between spaces (e.g. RGB ↔ YCbCr/YUV) via a fixed matrix applied independently to every pixel. Separates luma (brightness) from chroma (color-difference) so downstream stages can allocate less precision to the channels human vision is least sensitive to — the standard first step in most image and video codecs.
features: Per-pixel: transforms each pixel's channels independently of neighboring pixels
Decorrelates luma from chroma ahead of chroma subsampling and quantization
Reversible integer variants (e.g. subtract-green, JPEG 2000's RCT) vs. lossy floating-point variants (e.g. JPEG/ITU-R BT.601 YCbCr)
Standard first stage in JPEG, JPEG 2000, WebP, and most video codecs

papers.title: Studio encoding parameters of digital television for standard 4:3 and wide-screen 16:9 aspect ratios
papers.note: BT.601 — defines the RGB↔YCbCr conversion most image/video codecs use as their color-space transform

verification.notes: New module drafted for the image/video codec expansion (see docs/image-video-codec-scoping.md, Phase 1a). Not yet cross-checked against a specific implementation.

name: Adaptive Data Mapping
description: Adaptive Data Mapping (ADM): partitions a stream into fixed-size blocks, computes a per-block center (e.g. the block mean), and remaps each element to a compact code relative to that center — shrinking a wide integer stream (e.g. u16/u32) into a narrow symbol domain (e.g. 8-bit) before entropy coding. The narrower, more concentrated symbol distribution compresses substantially better under a subsequent entropy coder (e.g. ANS/Huffman) than the raw wide-integer stream.
features: Remaps wide integer codes into a compact symbol domain

papers.title: MANS: Efficient and Portable ANS Encoding for Multi-Byte Integer Data on CPUs and GPUs
papers.note: ADM stage as preprocessing for ANS entropy coding

verification.notes: generalized from FZGM implementation card; MANS paper citation still pending (repo-level attribution only)

name: Bit Shuffle (Transpose)
description: Transposes bits across values by collecting most significant bits together, then second most significant bits, and so on. Improves compressibility when values share similar bit patterns.
features: Improves compressibility for correlated bit positions

papers.title: LC Framework Documentation

name: Zigzag Ordering
description: Reorders multi-dimensional coefficients (typically from frequency transforms like DCT) in a zigzag pattern from low to high frequency. Creates roughly monotonically decreasing magnitude sequence, improving subsequent encoding efficiency. Not to be confused with zigzag encoding (see zigzag-encoding), a distinct, unrelated technique that shares only the name — it maps signed integers to unsigned integers rather than reordering coefficient positions.

papers.title: Fixed-Rate Compressed Floating-Point Arrays
papers.note: Zigzag ordering of DCT coefficients in ZFP

verification.notes: FZGM's ZigzagStage implementation entry moved to zigzag-encoding, 2026-07-07 (it was misassigned here — see that module's notes).

name: Burrows-Wheeler Transform (BWT)
description: Rearranges characters to group similar contexts together. Improves compressibility for subsequent encoding (used in bzip2).
features: Text-friendly but works on any data

papers.title: A Block-sorting Lossless Data Compression Algorithm

name: Tuple Shuffle
description: Rearranges k-tuples by grouping all first elements, then all second elements, etc. Benefits compression when values within the same dimension correlate more than across tuples.

papers.title: LC Framework Documentation

name: Axis Swizzle & Reshape
description: Permutes an array's axis order (e.g. transposing a [time, y, x] array to [y, x, time]) and/or reshapes it into a different rank/shape with the same element count, without touching any values. A pure layout change: it exists purely to place elements that later stages correlate well against (e.g. neighboring bytes, matching tuple positions) adjacent in memory ahead of them.
features: Pure layout change — no value modification, fully reversible
Axis permutation (transpose) and/or reshape to a different rank
Positions data for whatever correlation the next pipeline stage exploits
Configurable per target axis order / shape

verification.notes: Added as the technique behind numcodecs_wasm_swizzle_reshape; no dedicated paper (a general array-layout operation), no specific implementation confirmed beyond that codec.

name: Sorting
description: Pre-conditioning step that sorts data values in increasing order. Converts irregular spatial distributions into smooth monotonic curves, making subsequent curve fitting more accurate. Particularly effective for scientific data with high spatial irregularity.
features: Converts irregular data to monotonic curves

papers.title: ISABELA for Effective In Situ Compression of Scientific Data
papers.authors: S. Lakshminarasimhan, N. Shah, S. Ethier, S-H. Ku, C.S Chang, S. Klasky, R. Latham, R. Ross, N.F. Samatova

name: Run-Length Encoding (RLE)
description: Lossless compression that replaces sequences of repeated values with (value, count) pairs. Most effective for data with long runs of identical values.

papers.title: Run-Length Encoding

name: Repeat/Zero Elimination
description: Builds a bitmap flagging which words match a target value, emits only the non-matching words, and recursively compresses the bitmap itself. The zero-specialized variant (RZE) targets exactly zero; the general variant (RRE) matches any repeated value (e.g. the previous word). Same bitmap-and-compact structure, different match criterion.
features: Effective for sparse or repetitive data

papers.title: LC Framework Documentation

verification.notes: merged from rze-reducer + rre-reducer, 2026-07-05

name: Bit Packing
description: Packs data values into smaller bit widths than their native representation, eliminating unused high-order bits. Reduces storage size for data with small dynamic range.

papers.title: Bit Packing Methods

name: Bitplane Packing
description: Packs quantized integer values MSB-to-LSB into separate per-bit-significance streams (bitplanes), enabling progressive/refinable decoding -- higher-order planes can be decoded first for a coarse reconstruction, with lower-order planes added incrementally. Applies no compression by itself; downstream stages (RLE, entropy coding) exploit the resulting sparsity, especially in high-order planes.
features: No compression on its own -- reshapes data for downstream coders
Distinct from bit-packing's fixed-width repack and truncation's mantissa discard

papers.title: Progressive/Adaptable Retrieval via Multigrid Decomposition (PMGARD)
papers.note: Cited by FZ CPU Module Library as relying on MSB-to-LSB bitplane order for progressive retrieval

verification.notes: New module created 2026-07-13 from FZ CPU Module Library's catalog (BitplaneEncoder page); no exact prior Z-Hub module matched.

name: Compressed Leading-Zero Groups (CLOG)
description: Breaks data into subchunks and records the count of leading zero bits for each. Stores only the remaining significant bits, compressing values with many leading zeros. An adaptive variant additionally applies a TCMS (magnitude-sign) transform first to subchunks with no leading zeros, handling mixed bit patterns better than plain CLOG.
features: Efficient for values with common high-order bits

papers.title: LC Framework Documentation

name: Dictionary Encoding
description: Maps frequently occurring patterns to short codes using a dictionary/codebook, exploiting repeated sequences rather than per-value statistics. Classic LZ78/LZW-style dictionary coding; related to but distinct from LZ77's sliding-window matching.

papers.title: Compression of Individual Sequences via Variable-Rate Coding

name: LZ77 (Lempel-Ziv 1977)
description: Dictionary-based compression using sliding window. Replaces repeated sequences with back-references. Used in gzip, DEFLATE, Zstandard.

papers.title: A Universal Algorithm for Sequential Data Compression

name: Huffman Encoding
description: Variable-length entropy coding algorithm that assigns shorter codes to more frequent symbols. Builds a binary tree based on symbol frequencies for optimal prefix coding. Limited by integer bit lengths.

papers.title: A Method for the Construction of Minimum-Redundancy Codes

name: Arithmetic Coding
description: Entropy coding that represents entire message as single number in [0,1) interval. Achieves compression closer to theoretical entropy limit than Huffman coding.

papers.title: Arithmetic Coding for Data Compression
papers.authors: Witten I.H., Neal R.M., Cleary J.G.

name: Range Coding
description: Entropy coding similar to arithmetic coding but simpler. Maps input to subranges of [0,1) interval.

papers.title: Range Encoding

name: Asymmetric Numeral Systems (ANS)
description: Modern entropy coding combining speed of Huffman with compression of arithmetic coding. Used in Zstandard (FSE variant).

papers.title: Asymmetric Numeral Systems
Finite State Entropy

name: Adaptive Binning (ANS)
description: Entropy codes a stream of integers by grouping them into adaptively-sized bins (each covering a contiguous range with roughly equal probability mass), ANS-coding the bin index, then storing each value's offset within its bin as fixed-width bits. Converges quickly to the true entropy of smoothly, independently, identically distributed data without needing a full frequency table.
features: Converges close to true entropy for smooth i.i.d. integer distributions
Avoids building/transmitting a full per-symbol frequency table
Bin index coded with ANS; in-bin offset stored as raw bits

papers.note: Introduces the binning algorithm as Pco's core novel component

name: SPECK Coding
description: SPECK repeatedly tests large rectangular regions of wavelet coefficients for significance at descending bitplane thresholds, splitting only those regions that contain large values, and refining discovered coefficients progressively. Used as the coefficient coder in SPERR.

papers.title: Embedded and efficient low-complexity hierarchical image coder
papers.authors: W. A. Pearlman and A. Islam
papers.note: Introduced as a low complexity option for JPEG2000

papers.title: Embedded image coding using zeroblocks of subband/wavelet coefficients and context modeling
papers.note: higher complexity variant of SPECK, called (embedded zero block coding (EZBC))

papers.title: Efficient, low-complexity image coding with a set-partitioning embedded block coder
papers.authors: W.A. Pearlman, A. Islam, N. Nagaraj, A. Said

name: SPIHT Coding
description: Set Partitioning in Hierarchical Trees: codes wavelet coefficients by exploiting the tree structure across subbands (a coefficient's "descendants" at finer scales tend to be insignificant if it is), recursively partitioning sets of coefficients into significant/insignificant groups at descending bitplane thresholds and only subdividing sets that test significant. Predates and directly inspired SPECK's simpler rectangular-region variant.
features: Exploits parent-child insignificance correlation across wavelet subbands
Embedded/progressive bitstream — can be truncated at any point for a graceful quality/size tradeoff
No explicit tree pointers needed; decoder reconstructs the same partitioning

papers.title: A new, fast, and efficient image codec based on set partitioning in hierarchical trees
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology

verification.notes: Added as the residual-layer coder used by EBCC (see the ebcc composition); no specific Z-Hub-tracked implementation confirmed beyond that.

name: EBCOT
description: Context-adaptive embedded bitplane coder used by JPEG 2000. Partitions each wavelet subband into small, independently-coded code-blocks, then codes each bitplane in three passes (significance propagation, magnitude refinement, cleanup) where each bit's coding probability context is derived from the states of its already-coded neighbors and fed to a binary MQ arithmetic coder. Produces an embedded, quality-scalable bitstream that a post-compression rate-distortion optimization step can truncate per code-block to hit a target size or quality. Architecturally distinct from SPECK's set-partitioning approach (see speck-coding) — EBCOT uses fixed code-blocks with per-bit context modeling rather than SPECK's adaptive region-splitting.
features: Context-adaptive: each bit's coding probability depends on already-coded neighbor states
Fixed, independently-coded code-blocks (typically 64×64 or smaller), not global bitplane sets
Embeds a binary (MQ) arithmetic coder internally
Produces an embedded/scalable bitstream, truncatable per code-block for rate-distortion control

papers.title: High Performance Scalable Image Compression with EBCOT
papers.note: Original EBCOT algorithm, later adopted into JPEG 2000

papers.title: JPEG2000 Image Compression Fundamentals, Standards and Practice
papers.authors: David S. Taubman, Michael W. Marcellin
papers.note: Standard reference text covering EBCOT's role in JPEG 2000

verification.notes: New module drafted for the image/video codec expansion, Phase 1b (see docs/image-video-codec-scoping.md). Kept separate from speck-coding: speck-coding's own description is written narrowly around SPECK's set-partitioning mechanism; EBCOT's context-adaptive per-bit arithmetic coding over fixed code-blocks is a genuinely different algorithm, not a parameterization of SPECK. Marked lossless by the same reasoning as speck-coding: exact if run to full bitplane depth, lossy only if the rate-distortion step truncates it.

name: In-Loop Filter
description: Smooths reconstructed-frame artifacts (block-boundary discontinuities, ringing) using neighboring already-reconstructed pixels, running inside the compression loop itself: the filtered frame, not the raw decoded one, becomes the reference for future intra/inter prediction. Doesn't reduce data size and doesn't decorrelate for coding — its role is reference/output-quality repair rather than compression. Concrete forms vary by codec: H.264's deblocking filter, HEVC's deblocking + Sample Adaptive Offset (SAO), AV1's Constrained Directional Enhancement Filter (CDEF) + loop restoration, and H.266/VVC's Adaptive Loop Filter (ALF).
features: Operates on already-reconstructed pixels using their neighbors, after the transform/quantize/entropy stages
In-loop: filtered output feeds back as the reference for future prediction, not just decoder-side cosmetic cleanup
Doesn't compress and doesn't decorrelate for coding — a distinct pipeline role from the other six categories
Concrete form varies by codec (deblocking, SAO, CDEF, loop restoration, ALF)
